# Intake graph tables, in plain language

<!-- Generated by: Codex | Date: 2026-09-12 | Rev: 1 | Platform: Codex / win32 -->

This describes migration `0001_filesystem_graph.surql`: 14 node tables (things)
and 19 relation tables (links between things). Schema deployment does not mean
the source collection has been loaded. These are Intake organization records,
not downstream evidence acceptance or instructions to move or delete files.

## The essential distinction

An **occurrence** is a particular file observed at a particular source path.
**Content** is its exact-byte identity, established by SHA-256. Two occurrences
may point at the same content without either occurrence being removed. Two files
with the same name but different sizes or hashes remain different observations;
a name match is a lead to investigate, not proof of duplication or corruption.

## Node tables

| Table | What it represents |
|---|---|
| `store` | A storage boundary and its source location, such as an explicitly identified local root or cloud source. |
| `occurrence` | A file/directory observation with raw path, normalized path, name, observed size and timestamps. Support in the schema does not imply every importer emits directory rows. |
| `content` | One verified exact-byte identity and byte size, independent of where copies occur. |
| `representation` | A rendering, parse, sidecar or alternate format, without pretending different formats are identical bytes. |
| `atomic_unit` | A directory/container to keep together, including messy nested roots; its published basis is recorded. |
| `subject_account` | A source-supported account identity. This allows different Takeout accounts to remain separate. |
| `export_event` | One distinct export event, so several exports from an account do not silently become one. |
| `archive_series` | A multipart archive set, with unknown/incomplete/complete status and optional expected count. |
| `archive_part` | An observed original ZIP/archive part, its filename, occurrence and optional part number. |
| `identity_assertion` | A proposed account attribution with supporting signals and confidence, not an established fact. |
| `machine_proposal` | A proposed duplicate, extraction relationship or other machine conclusion, with rationale and producing run. |
| `review_decision` | A human decision with reviewer, time and reason. Corrections are separate linked decisions. |
| `operation_run` | Which tool execution produced work, when it ran and its status/receipt. |
| `projection_snapshot` | The manifest/checkpoint provenance for a graph projection. A completed load must not be inferred merely from this record's existence. |

## Relation tables

| Table | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stored_at` | Occurrence → store. |
| `occurrence_has_content` | Occurrence → verified exact content. |
| `represents` | Representation → exact content identity. |
| `member_of` | Occurrence/representation/archive part → atomic unit. |
| `contains` | Direct parent container → child; nested containers remain nested. |
| `originated_from` | Source-supported origin → export event or archive part. |
| `part_of_series` | Archive part → multipart series. |
| `belongs_to_account` | Source-supported export/series/unit → account. |
| `produced_by` | Snapshot → producing run. |
| `proposes_subject_for` | Identity assertion → object being attributed. |
| `proposal_subject` | Proposal → its subject object. |
| `proposal_object` | Proposal → its comparison/target object. |
| `possible_extraction_of` | Proposed extraction lineage, retaining the proposal and uncertainty. |
| `corroborates` | Proposed corroboration; distinct supporting sources stay distinct. |
| `alternate_representation_of` | Proposed alternative rendition/format, not an exact-byte claim. |
| `proposed_duplicate_of` | Proposed duplicate occurrence/unit pair; never a deletion instruction. |
| `decides_on` | Human decision → machine proposal or identity assertion. |
| `confirms_extraction` | Human acceptance → proposed extraction link. |
| `supersedes_decision` | New human decision → earlier decision it corrects. |

## How this fits the recovery work

For Takeout, keep account, export event, multipart series, original archive parts
and extracted roots distinguishable. Unknown ownership/completeness stays unknown;
folder-name or content clues become proposals until their basis is established.
For Facebook, keep nested atomic roots intact. Stray thread folders, payment or
account-center folders, off-Facebook app folders and FB_IMG files are investigation
leads if outside a proper unit, not automatic extraction targets.

The graph can describe candidate best copies and missing-file differences. It
does not itself select files for B2, flatten exports, migrate every message thread,
or authorize a physical move. B2 is the consolidation destination, not a mirror
whose duplicate copies should be preserved indiscriminately.

The schema enforces types and relation endpoint types. Append-only review and
immutable projection behavior also require disciplined backend write paths; the
database-scoped EDITOR credential is not a fine-grained human-approval mechanism.

See [deployment proof](SURREAL-INTAKE-DEPLOYMENT-2026-09-12.md) for what is live and
[MASTER-TODO](MASTER-TODO.md) for the remaining projection/rebuild gates.
